mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically across the last three weekly means (-64.6, -61.6, -60.1), a persistent stabilization slope after the t-2w trough. Extrapolating this three-week drift implies the next 28-day average exceeds the last 28-day average.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly means -64.6, -61.6, -60.1 over t-2w, t-1w, t-0w
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to the last 28-day mean (-61.55), showing the three-week stabilization slope does not persist.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL sits at +16.4 percent above baseline and has stayed above +16 in all four weekly means, indicating discretionary time is still anchored at home. Sustained home-anchoring drains Manhattan retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean remains above +15 percent above baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean rises above the last 28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above +15 in every week of the window.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has recovered 6.8 points off its t-2w low (-34.1 to -27.3), showing essential-trip normalization. When essential errands recover by more than 5 points off the four-week low, households re-add non-essential errands within two weeks and lift RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 5 points above its trailing 4-week minimum
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -34.1 at t-2w to -27.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stays more than 5 points above its four-week low for two weeks yet RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean falls below its trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS rebounded sharply from -47.9 to -38.0 week-on-week, a 9.9-point jump, showing outdoor discretionary trips are resuming. When outdoor leisure demand crosses above -40, adjacent street-level retail captures part of that footfall within one week, raising RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean crosses above -40 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS weekly mean moved from -47.9 at t-1w to -38.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the week immediately following a PARKS print above -40 is lower than the trailing four-week RETAIL_REC mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT (-55.9) and WORKPLACES (-47.1) are both deeply depressed and neither has recovered past its t-3w level. Manhattan retail footfall requires the joint inflow of commuters and office workers; with both below -45 simultaneously, the consumer pool stays absent and RETAIL_REC declines.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain more than 45 points below baseline at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean rises above its trailing 28-day mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain below -45.

mechanism_narrative: High RESIDENTIAL (+16.4) combined with a recovering PARKS reading (-38.0) means discretionary time is being routed to neighborhood outdoor space rather than retail corridors. The joint condition caps retail re-engagement over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above +15 and PARKS above -42 at the same weekly observation
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL +16.4 and PARKS -38.0 co-occur at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean exceeds its trailing 28-day mean in weeks where RESIDENTIAL is above +15 and PARKS is above -42.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening second-wave restrictions, a WORKPLACES drop of more than 5 points week-on-week signals fresh capacity caps or remote-work mandates. Retail venues are curtailed within days, dragging RETAIL_REC lower in the following week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points below its prior weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 5.8 points from t-3w to t-2w alongside RETAIL_REC's trough
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES drops more than 5 points week-on-week, RETAIL_REC in the following week is equal to or above its prior weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: The 28-day window spans the holiday peak and the January collapse. With RETAIL_REC already at -60.1 and GROCERY_PHARM only partially recovered at -27.3, the post-holiday seasonal trough outweighs the late-December lift, pulling the forward 28-day mean below the trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: calendar window includes at least two weeks after 1 January
evidence_refs: fact:decision point 2020-12-15 places the 28-day window across late December and January
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the 28 days after 2020-12-15 is greater than or equal to the trailing 28-day mean of -61.55.
